headline: Record revenue, expanding margins, strong forward outlook
summary_short: Lam Research reported fiscal Q4 2026 (June-quarter) revenue of $6.722 billion, up 30.0% y/y and 15.1% q/q — a company record — with GAAP diluted EPS of $1.81 (+34.1% y/y) and operating margin of 37.4% (+370bps y/y); the company guided the September quarter to $8.10B +/- $400M revenue.
summary_long: Revenue rose 30.0% y/y (+15.1% q/q) to $6.722B, which management attributes to AI-driven demand reshaping the semiconductor industry and Lam's technology-leadership investments helping customers manage rising manufacturing complexity. GAAP operating margin expanded to 37.4% (+370bps y/y) as opex grew only 13.8% y/y against 30% revenue growth; net income grew slower (+32.4% y/y) than operating income (+44.4% y/y) because the effective tax rate rose to ~10.9% from ~3.3%. Diluted EPS was $1.81 GAAP / $1.82 non-GAAP. Cash rose to $5.579B (+17.4% q/q) on operating cash flow, net of $246.6M of buybacks and $325.3M of dividends. Lam guided the September quarter to $8.10B +/- $400M revenue and $2.15 +/- $0.15 diluted EPS, both increases versus June.

drivers.explanation: CEO cites AI-driven demand reshaping the semiconductor industry and Lam's technology leadership helping customers manage rising manufacturing complexity.
Margin expansion is fully explained by revenue growing 30.0% y/y while total operating expenses grew only 13.8% y/y.
Net income growth (+32.4% y/y) trails operating-income growth (+44.4% y/y) because the effective tax rate rose to ~10.9% from ~3.3% a year ago.
Tracks net income growth, aided modestly by a ~1.6% y/y reduction in diluted share count from buybacks.

Cash fell 12.7% y/y despite $5.858B TTM operating cash flow, because $3.851B of TTM buybacks and $1.271B of TTM dividends exceeded it; q/q, cash rose on stronger in-quarter operating cash flow per the release.

Not explained in the release; per our own balance-sheet reconciliation (see confidence_notes) this y/y decline doesn't match the release's own flat 'long-term debt and finance lease' line — likely an upstream data-tagging artifact, not an actual paydown.

A $751.194M debt principal repayment recorded in the March-2026-quarter cash flow retired most of the $754.311M current-portion balance carried at June 2025, leaving $4.073M current portion by June 2026 per the release.
Equity growth is explained by $2.277B of quarterly net income added to retained earnings, exceeding $246.6M of buybacks and $325.3M of dividends returned to shareholders in the quarter.
CEO Tim Archer: record revenue, operating margin, and EPS in the June quarter on AI-driven demand, positioning Lam for a third consecutive year of outperformance in 2026.
